stem: A nurse practices outside the legal scope authorized by the applicable Nurse Practice Act. Which regulatory consequence is possible?

options.A: The board of nursing may impose discipline such as remediation, practice restrictions, suspension, or revocation, depending on applicable law and the facts of the case.
options.B: The consequence is limited to employer counseling because boards of nursing do not enforce Nurse Practice Acts.
options.C: Every scope violation automatically results in permanent license revocation regardless of severity, facts, or jurisdiction.
options.D: Every scope violation automatically produces a criminal conviction before any regulatory investigation or board proceeding occurs.

rationale: NCSBN explains that state boards of nursing enforce nursing laws and may take disciplinary action when a violation is established. Available board actions vary with state law and the facts and can include remediation or education, reprimand/fines, monitoring or probation, practice restrictions, suspension, and revocation or voluntary surrender. Therefore A is correct. B incorrectly denies board authority, while C and D falsely make one severe outcome automatic for every scope violation without investigation, due process, or jurisdiction-specific law.
educational_objective: Recognize that practicing outside legal nursing scope can lead to board-of-nursing discipline, with sanctions determined by the applicable Nurse Practice Act, jurisdiction, facts, severity, and disciplinary process rather than an automatic single penalty.

source_original.stem: A nurse practices outside the legal scope authorized by the applicable Nurse Practice Act. Which consequence is possible?

options.A: Board-of-nursing discipline is possible and may include remediation, restrictions, suspension, or revocation depending on law and the facts.
options.B: The consequence is limited to employer counseling because Nurse Practice Acts are not enforced by boards of nursing.
options.C: A scope violation automatically produces permanent license revocation regardless of severity or jurisdiction.
options.D: A scope violation automatically produces a criminal conviction before any regulatory investigation occurs.

source_original.rationale: Boards of nursing enforce Nurse Practice Acts to protect the public. NCSBN describes disciplinary actions that may include remediation, restrictions, suspension, or revocation; the exact sanction depends on state law and the facts of the case.
source_original.source_detail: Board disciplinary actions may restrict practice, suspend a license, or revoke/surrender a license Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15. correction_summary: Retained the legal-scope/discipline construct and key A, explicitly framed the answer as a possible regulatory consequence rather than a guaranteed outcome, strengthened the jurisdiction/state-law caveat, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the final item tests a direct nursing-regulation principle.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Nurse Practice Act scope violation and board discipline
audit_findings.source_authority: Current NCSBN nursing-regulation guidance; NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: NCSBN Board Action, Discipline, and NPA Toolkit pages live-rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.exact_locator: NCSBN Board Action > Disciplinary Actions; Discipline complaint-to-resolution process; NPA Toolkit authority framework
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item accurately presents discipline as possible and variable by jurisdiction/facts, avoiding automatic revocation or criminal-conviction claims and avoiding a state-specific sanction prediction.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because BONs have regulatory authority over alleged Nurse Practice Act violations.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because sanction type varies and revocation is not automatic for every violation.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because a board regulatory process does not automatically create a criminal conviction before investigation.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A reflects the variable, jurisdiction-dependent disciplinary framework without asserting an automatic outcome.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address consequences of the same scope violation; the correct response depends on regulatory process rather than wording length alone.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care — legal scope, professional limitations and regulatory responsibility.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current NCSBN Board Action, Discipline, and NPA Toolkit guidance, all four alternatives, rationale, objective, legal-certainty language, ambiguity, cueing and Management of Care mapping. A remained uniquely correct.
